content: What does it mean that success is as dangerous as failure? Whether you go up the ladder or down it, your position is shaky.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching (Dao De Jing), Book of the Way
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Across his life and work, Lao Tzu saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
